acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Harpies family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Sky Queen, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Four-Perch Storm-Court Sovereign (Sovereign) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Storm-purple and white wings span the cliff arena, the crest forms a full crown, gold cuffs ring every limb, and a family-native non-affinity halo of loose feathers orbits only the physical wing beats.

Signature mechanic: Court of Four Cliffs: the Sky Queen spans opposite perches with storm-colored wings and assigns a Screecher, Talon, Skyrender, or Matriarch to each gold-cuffed ledge. One crown feather names the active courtier, whose familiar mechanic establishes a lane; the Queen then closes one wing across it. Destroying the exposed cuff anchor drops that perch, dismisses its courtier, and tears one long primary from the Queen's span. At two remaining perches she must land between commands; at one she loses the loose-feather halo and fights with short committed talon sweeps.
battlefieldDuty: Command a cliff-arena boss across four destructible perches, composing every lower-form lane before successive perch breaks force closer, simpler phases.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe attachments: T1–T3 mount shell valves and narrow skin reservoirs on braided rawhide straps beside talons and wing roots; T4–T5 integrate those valves into gold ankle rings and gold cuffs without changing the earlier status silhouette.
Flight shows coherent filling and release: specific feathers darken as reservoirs charge, narrow cutting sheets leave the selected edge, wet reflections track flow, and drainage exposes the valve.
counterplay: Use the selected lower form's learned safe response, then strike the revealed cuff anchor while the spanning wing is committed; every broken perch permanently removes one command and narrows the Queen's reach. Affinity signal: T1–T3 lift a shell valve on a rawhide talon strap as connected feathers darken; T4–T5 lift that valve from a gold ankle ring or gold cuff, and every tier exposes the drained matte wing edge after release.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only blue plumage without reservoirs, valves, and wet-surface change
Glow-only water treatment without coherent filling, release, and drainage
Liquid wings that erase feather anatomy
Spray that obscures the wing-root or talon telegraph
identityInvariants: A humanoid torso remains joined to large raptor wings that replace or extend the arms, backward-jointed bird legs, oversized talons, and a feathered head crest.
Slate grey, brown, and dirty cream mature into iridescent blue-green, storm purple, and white without losing the family feather pattern.
Feather, hollow bone, sinew, raw hide, braided hair, and gold ankle ornaments remain physically readable materials.
Bone jewelry, trophy feathers, braided hair, ankle rings, and crest height communicate status without changing the core wing-and-talon silhouette.
Every attack keeps the wing roots, talons, crest, and flight direction visible enough to preserve counterplay.
telegraph: The full crest-crown raises one named feather, a matching gold cuff rings against its perch, ordinary loose feathers align around the selected lower form, and one enormous wing unfolds across the announced lane.
